title: Story card
description: One story card in data/story/<id>.json (S1-S4): one or two sentences in the game's tone, shown at a fixed moment of the run. Templated names ({yokai}, {move}) are filled from the player's run (S4); every placeholder used in title or text must be listed in placeholders, and every listed one used.

trigger.description: When the card shows (the S3 schedule entry it implements).

title.description: Optional heading shown above the text.

placeholders.description: Run names the game fills in (S4): {yokai} = the yokai's display name, {move} = the copy target's move name.

speaker.description: Who says it, e.g. Ryo, narrator, Master Soen, Tanuki.

later_loss.description: YOK-212 (S3): marks a later-loss wake-up card. It shows when Ryo loses on a map row from row_min to row_max (both included; the default map puts the Tanuki on row 9) to the named yokai; an elder counts as its yokai (elder-oni = oni). Left out = not a later-loss card. The game picks a card naming the yokai, else one naming none (the row band), else lose-screen; ties: narrower row range, then lower id in ordinal text order (so x-10 comes before x-2). A later-loss card fills only {yokai}. tools/validate_data.py also checks what the schema can't: row_min <= row_max, rows written as plain integers (4, not 4.0 or 1e1), placeholders.

yokai.description: The yokai that won: the plain yokai id, as a loss carries it (NodeContext.DraftYokai); an elder, the apprentice and the Nine-Tails count as their yokai. Same list as StoryLibrary's LaterLoss.Winners. Left out = any yokai: the row band's card.
